claims.object_text: novel physical and functional interaction between DAT and Kv2.1
claims.quote: we describe a novel physical and functional interaction between DAT and the voltage-gated K+ channel Kv2.1 (potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily B member 1 or KCNB1).
Kv2.1 is trafficked to membrane-bound clusters observed both in vivo and in vitro in rodent dopamine neurons.

claims.object_text: decrease DAT's lateral mobility and inhibit its internalization
claims.quote: clustered Kv2.1 channels decrease DAT's lateral mobility and inhibit its internalization,

claims.object_text: decreasing canonical transporter activity by altering DAT's conformational equilibrium
claims.quote: while also decreasing canonical transporter activity by altering DAT's conformational equilibrium.

claims.object_text: Kv2.1 clusters exert a spatially discrete homeostatic braking mechanism on DAT
claims.quote: Kv2.1 clusters exert a spatially discrete homeostatic braking mechanism on DAT by inducing a relative increase in inward-facing transporters.

claims.object_text: alterations in the functional interaction between DAT and Kv2.1 affect dopamine neuron activity
claims.quote: it is possible that alterations in the functional interaction between DAT and Kv2.1 affect dopamine neuron activity.
